newsitem.title: INDIA: TEXT-India SEBI statement after board meeting.
newsitem.headline: TEXT-India SEBI statement after board meeting.

text.p: Following is the text of a statement issued by the Securities and Exchange Board of India (SEBI) after a meeting of its board of directors on Tuesday:

"SEBI board today considered the status of Capital Market. While taking note of the decline, it was felt that SEBI's role in the matter would be limited to further improving regulatory aspects, towards which several steps had either been taken or were in the process of being taken.

The Board also considered the issue of permitting rights issues of mutual funds. It was felt that in the cases of close-ended schemes, rights issues could be permitted, provided the existing unit holders were given repurchase facility at net asset value (NAV) related price. This would effectively protect the interests of investors.

Further, the Board considered the policy regarding grant of recognition to new stock exchanges. The Board was of the view that on account of technological changes and infrastructural and other costs involved, requests for opening new stock exchanges were likely to be limited. However, considering the existing legal provisions contained in Securities Contracts (Regulation) Act, 1956, SEBI, without prohibiting recognition of new stock exchanges could regulate the grant of recognition. In view of these factors, it was decided that recognition, if considered necessary in public interest and that of trade could be allowed subject to the following conditions.
- The exchange begins trading only after introduction of on-line screen-based trading.
- The exchange makes rules, regulations and by-laws with adequate provisions for investor protection with the approval of SEBI and thereafter strictly follows them.
- The exchange establishes a Clearing House within six months from date of recognition."
